property_summary: After a successful initialize(_baseToken, ...), the stored base token always equals the _baseToken argument passed in (c.baseToken() == _baseToken); the mutant stores _nft instead, so it violates this whenever _baseToken != _nft.
After any successful initialize call, c.baseToken() must equal the _baseToken argument passed in; the mutant stores address(0) instead, so any call with a nonzero _baseToken breaks the rule.

After any successful initialize with an ERC20 base token of d decimals (4<=d<=36, d!=18), c.price() must equal virtualBaseTokenReserves * 10**(36-d) / virtualNftReserves; the mutant stores address(0) as baseToken so it wrongly uses the native-token exponent of 18 and returns a different price.
